Whose preferences? Planner-dependent cost recovery

Whose preferences? — recovering a reaching cost with different planners

A 3-link arm reaches from its home rest posture to a target point under a 6-feature cost with known weights w*. One planner generates a demo; each planner then recovers the weights that explain it. Same task, same features — only the planner differs. All three planners (exact OCP, calibrated MPPI-full, receding-horizon MPPI-recede) serve as both demo and recoverer, so the fair own-generator diagonal is visible.

Panel 2 · time-varying weights w(t)

Now the preference changes across the reach — a smooth w(t) curve (a 6-bump basis). The demo determines only part of it, so each feature's curve carries a shaded identifiability band: narrow where the demo pins w(t) (trustworthy), wide where it's free (the equivalence class). Full demo × planner grid; each planner graded on its own-generator demo, and the receding planner sees only a short lookahead window of w(t).
